blocks.text: The shape of a thoughtful pause

A page begins to speak before we read its first sentence. The width of a column, the space between lines, and the quiet around a heading tell us how to approach it. Those relationships change with the words, the typeface, and the screen. A useful tool should make that change visible while leaving room for judgment.

Consider a heading enlarged by a few points. It may cross a wrapping threshold, add a line, and pull the paragraph below it down the page. The right response may involve a wider measure, a smaller gap, or simply accepting the new rhythm. No single ratio can settle that choice.

preferences.source: caller ranges and local hue-wheel convention

assumptions: Opaque encoded sRGB inputs; no alpha, blending, gradients, images, HDR or Display P3.
WCAG luminance is not OKLab lightness. Contrast is not a complete accessibility audit.
No role declarations means no contrast obligations were checked; it is not an accessibility pass.
Hue-wheel preferences are optional descriptors, not physical constraints or a beauty score.

alignment.preferenceSource: caller tolerance; no universal alignment target is inferred

hierarchy.interpretation: box area and declared priority are not font weight, perceived emphasis, comprehension or task importance

balance.interpretation: geometric occupied-area center, not salience-weighted visual balance; asymmetry is not a defect

whitespace.interpretation: unoccupied supplied rectangle area, not glyph-ink whitespace; clipping and union prevent double counting

overlap.interpretation: pairwise intersections; intentional layering and parent/child containment are not automatically errors

readingOrder.interpretation: geometric reversals relative to declared axis/direction only; not DOM, focus, screen-reader or multi-column order validation

provenance.geometry: deterministic axis-aligned rectangle calculations; source measurement quality remains the caller responsibility
provenance.judgment: none: no preference rating, universal beauty score, or optimization target

limitations: Supply comparable semantic regions; including a full-surface container makes its area occupied by definition.
Union occupancy/centroid are invariant to duplicate nested coverage; pairwise alignment/proximity and area hierarchy are not.
No glyph ink, color salience, occlusion order, gaze, semantics, motion or interaction is inferred from boxes.
Geometry can describe grouping and rhythm, but human task context determines whether they work.
No layout is emitted; any downstream implementation must preserve the project flex/Yoga-only contract.
